subject: Activation: BridgeFlow streaming + JSON gateway — kickoff & schema alignment
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@healthexample.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Greer <tom.greer@healthexample.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Oct 2029 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: BridgeFlow activation — streaming + JSON outputs (next steps)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — Tom and I are ready to move BridgeFlow into a limited pilot that uses the streaming API with function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. We want to scope the minimal set of events and the output schema so our engineering team can wire the downstream ingestion.

Two main asks to get to the pilot:
- A mutual action plan with owner assignments and target dates.
- A first-pass JSON schema for the structured output and guidance on prefix/KV caching tradeoffs for low-latency streaming.

Can you help coordinate a 45‑minute kickoff this week? We prefer Wed or Thu morning US ET.

Thanks,
Sarah
Product Lead, HealthExample

Attachment: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@healthexample.com>, Tom Greer <tom.greer@healthexample.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Oct 2029 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow activation — streaming + JSON outputs (next steps)

Hi Sarah, Tom — great to hear you’re ready. Happy to run the kickoff. Ive attached an initial mutual action plan and a first-pass schema draft for the structured output. Quick notes up front:

- Pilot scope: streaming transcripts + a single function call for "diagnosis_rerank"; structured JSON should contain meta, events[], and a final summary object.
- Latency targets: aim for median tail < 350ms for token stream; rely on prefix caching for repeated session prompts. Marcus will cover runtime checks and caching knobs. Monica will own schema validation and acceptance tests.

Proposed slots: Wed 2029-10-23 10:30 ET or Thu 2029-10-24 09:30 ET. Which works for your team?

Attachments:
- HE-BridgeFlow-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan, owners & dates)
- bridgeflow-json-schema-draft-vA.json (schema first pass)
- runbook-runtime-checks.pdf (what Marcus will review)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@healthexample.com>, Tom Greer <tom.greer@healthexample.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Oct 2029 02:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow activation — streaming + JSON outputs (next steps)

Looping in early tech notes from my side — posting so we have clear tradeoffs for the kickoff: 

- Streaming + function calls: we should bind the function signature to a small, deterministic schema to avoid type regressions. If HealthExample expects >1 function we’ll need canary routing.
- KV caching: useful if sessions re-use long prompts (e.g., patient history). Recommend starting with a 5‑minute sliding TTL and a conservative max cache size (per-customer) to prevent memory pressure during peak.
- Quantization/latency: for pilot we recommend FP16 on p4d for stable latency; if they want lower cost later we can test int8 variants but expect slightly higher variance.

I will prepare a short checklist to run in the kickoff (environment checks, warm-up spike, sample payloads + schema conformance). Attaching the runbook I referenced.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-runtime-checks.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Oct 2029 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow activation — streaming + JSON outputs (next steps)

Thanks Marcus — adding a couple of schema-validation items so the acceptance test is actionable:

- Schema conformance suite (JSON Schema draft-07): sample positives/negatives + expected error codes.
- Tool-call contract: define required fields for the function input (patient_id, event_ts, input_tokens_limit) and the expected output union types.
- CI gating: well run the conformance suite against a test harness (HealthExample to provide a small dataset).

Ill add these to the MAP and flag owners.

—Monica
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 24 Oct 2029 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow activation — streaming + JSON outputs (next steps)

All — Wed 10:30 ET works for us. Sarah is looping in two engineers (cc below) who will bring sample payloads. Weve reviewed the MAP and the schema draft; were fine with the MVP fields but would like a short pre-kickoff checklist for the network and auth callouts so our infra team can open firewall rules ahead of time.

Also, quick Q on payload size: our typical event is ~2.3KB before encoding. Any guidance on websocket frame size or chunking best-practice?

Appreciate it — see you Wednesday.

Tom Greer
Engineering Manager, HealthExample
